newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Hepworth bucks weak building markets.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Hepworth bucks weak building markets.

text.p: British heating and building materials group Hepworth Plc reported only a modest decline in interim pre-tax profits on Friday, bucking the trends which have seen sharp falls in profits across the sector.

Hepworth's first-half pre-tax profit of 35.5 million pounds ($55.4 million), compared with 37.5 million a year before, was ahead of market forecasts, although the group chose cautiously to leave its dividend payout unchanged at 5.5 pence per share.
The results were set against a background of tough market conditions, with a weak housing market, sharp falls in new road projects and sluggish continental economies all depressing its performance.

Similar market conditions saw interim pre-tax profits at larger rivals Redland plunge 42 percent to 95 million, while RMC Group saw its half-year profits drop 27 percent to 95.8 million when they reported earlier this month.

Hepworth's shares however failed to sparkle, with news of the departure of a key manager worrying some analysts. The share was down 3p to 287 around midday after Hepworth said Jean-Francois Chene is to stand down as head of its French heating business, Saunier Duval.

"Markets have been quite tough," chief executive John Carter said in an interview, attributing Hepworth's relatively "robust" performance to the impact of efficiency gains and a focus on international markets.
"We have improved to the point where we can export internationally, and that is going on across all parts of the group," he said.
The firm's British operations exported more than a quarter of their output, with first-half exports up 24 percent to 66 million.
Carter said Hepworth's sights are set firmly on further expansion in eastern Europe and China as it seeks growth through new markets and new products.
Hepworth is in advanced talks about a number of projects in China, where it is already building two factories to make gas boilers and mains water pipes.
"We are at the detailed planning stages on a number of initiatives and that it all I can say," Carter said.
Hepworth is particularly keen to expand its pipes business in China, with its system of flexible, plastic plumbing products high on the list.
"The infrastructure demand in China continues developing at a very strong pace and we want to introduce all our new innovative technology in China," he said.

Hepworth "wants to get China right," but is also interested in moving into other parts of south-east Asia. In eastern Europe, Carter said the group plans to expand from its base in Poland into neighboring countries in the next six to 12 months, through greenfield projects, joint ventures and acquisitions.
"Heating is our spearhed project," he said. ($1=.6405 Pound)
